introduction.text: The Aula dei Mensores is a Roman collegial hall in Ostia that housed grain measurers, illustrating the administrative infrastructure of the ancient city.

history.description: The Aula was originally built during the Trajanic period, around 112 AD, as indicated by its earliest opus latericium and mixtum walls.
Later, in the late Severan period, the Aula underwent brick modifications and added new pillars, reflecting changes in Roman architectural styles.

design.description: The hall is roughly rectangular, accessed via a seven‑metre wide entrance on Via della Foce. Its walls were originally supported by a perimeter wall on the west and north sides and pillars attached to the west wall and east side; later the wall thickness was doubled and additional pillars were added.

art.description: A black‑and‑white mosaic with blue tesserae on the floor depicts mensores frumentarii measuring grain, including figures pointing to numbers and using a counting rod with nine tablets, a typical Severan decorative motif.
